title: Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan: college plans lost to a good paying job
summary: Playing a cafe in Moose Jaw, he is befriended by white kids, plays basketball at the YMCA, registers for college, but takes the band money instead and never goes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: What was your first long trip where you came out to really stay, where you realized...?
Well, I left... See, I was supposed to go to college. And I even sent for all my credits when I was in Moose Jaw. We played a little cafe in Moose Jaw...
Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan. That's in Canada.

So we played this... Boy, and I was inexperienced... I could sing a little bit, but I didn't... And I was so young. All the kids used to come on account of me being in the band. Because I went and joined the YMCA, because I was just fresh out of high school and I could play pretty good basketball... I'm trying to think of the name them kids gave me. Bill. I don't know where they got that name, but they couldn't think of (?), and they just was all White, see... So they give me the name of Bill. And they took me to their homes and took me... One day they took me to church. I had a great experience with them.

And I had aspirations to go to college. So I sent for my credits, and registered in the college in Moose Jaw. But when September come, I was making more money than I'd ever made. So I said, "Well, I'll wait, and go next semester." But they had taught us in high school if you miss that first semester, it's a possibility you'll never make college, and that's just what happened.
